profile.reading: This is the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts data center at the Bologna Technopole, built on the 13 hectare grounds of a former state tobacco factory in Bologna, Italy. ECMWFs member states council selected Bologna to host the centers new data center on June 22, 2017, and the facility was intended to be completed by the second quarter of 2019, occupying three of five surviving vaulted brick industrial structures known locally as the Botti, designed for a projected 60 year operational lifespan. The Emilia-Romagna regional government provided the land, the existing historic building, and its full renovation to ECMWF at no cost for the duration of the hosting agreement. The site was engineered with two fully rated 10 megawatt electrical circuits, upgradeable to 20 megawatts, to support supercomputers delivering roughly ten times ECMWFs prior computational capacity, enabling the centers push toward 5 kilometer grid resolution ensemble weather forecasts by 2025, down from about 18 kilometers previously. ECMWF is an independent intergovernmental organization supported by more than 30 European member and cooperating states that produces global numerical weather predictions used across the continent. ECMWF was founded in 1975 and remains headquartered in Reading, Berkshire, in the United Kingdom, operating this Bologna site as part of a multi site structure rather than a full relocation. The Bologna facility houses an Atos BullSequana XH2000 supercomputer system procured under a service contract worth more than 80 million euros, comprising 7,680 AMD Epyc Rome compute nodes plus 448 GPU accelerated nodes, over 1,040,000 total cores, 2.1 pebibytes of total memory, direct liquid cooling, and an HDR InfiniBand network delivering more than 300 terabits per second of bisection bandwidth per cluster. The Bologna system took over production of ECMWFs operational global weather forecasts on October 18, 2022. ECMWF also serves as the European Unions entrusted entity for two Copernicus programs run partly from this site, the Copernicus Atmosphere Monitoring Service and the Copernicus Climate Change Service, and has partnered with Italys Cineca on adopting technology for the EUs Destination Earth digital twin initiative.
